//ConnectionStrings: The roadplan asks for SQL Server authentication, which is the form below: a SQL login, not
the Windows account. It needs a real SQL Server (Developer edition or a container) — point
Server= at it and create the login there.
The LocalDB fallback is kept for a machine with no SQL Server installed. LocalDB supports no
SQL authentication at all, only the Windows account that owns the instance, so it cannot
satisfy the roadplan on this point:
Either way the password does not belong in this file once the database is not local — set
ConnectionStrings__ArgusDatabase as an environment variable instead; it overrides this.
//WindowsAuth: Windows (Negotiate) sign-in next to the username + password form. Off by default: it needs
the API hosted on a domain-joined Windows machine, and a browser asked to negotiate against
a server that cannot answer just fails. With Enabled=false the sign-in screen hides the
A domain account signs in as the Argus user whose WindowsAccountName matches it (DOMAIN\user,
case-insensitive), mapped on the Users screen. AutoProvisionUsers creates that user on the
first sign-in instead of refusing — only turn it on where domain membership is the
authorisation, since it makes every account that can reach the URL an Argus user.
//Seed: InstallationCount is how many installations the demo grid should hold. The seeder only
tops the table up to it and never deletes, so 0 leaves just the hand-written demo rows.
//AuditLog: The action log: one line per API request in logs/argus-actions.log, formatted
[timestamp] [action] [command] [status] [actor], where command is the request as it was sent
and actor is the signed-in user with the way they signed in — 'jnovak (Windows)'.
RetentionDays deletes anything older; set it to 0 to keep every file forever.
